gaps.1: And almost every single attempt ended in a small disaster. Cracked jars, scorched brown wax, and a kitchen that smelled like burning chemicals.
gaps.2: So the wax just sits there, holding a calm, steady, safe temperature the whole time.
gaps.3: So the temperature does not gently climb. It rockets, straight past the point where wax can catch fire.
gaps.4: And you can watch the smoke start lifting off the surface as it breaks down.
gaps.5: So one pocket is boiling and smoking while the rest is barely soft. There is no even, gentle melt.
gaps.6: That uneven stress builds until a crack spreads right across the glass, and it splits.
gaps.7: You add your oil, it hisses against the overheated wax, and half of it is gone before it even mixes in.
gaps.8: Any of those gets you real speed without the smoke, the cracking, or the dead fragrance.
gaps.9: That cooling window, watching the thermometer drift down to your number, is exactly the control a microwave erases.
gaps.10: Every single thick-versus-thin glass test ended the same way, with a crack somewhere in the jar.
gaps.11: Pour too hot and the candle sinks in the middle as it cools, leaving an ugly crater around the wick.
gaps.12: A jar that looks perfectly melted on top can still be way too hot underneath, like this one.
gaps.13: A cracked, scorched mess on one side, and a clean, glossy, great-smelling candle on the other.
